newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian court condemns eight Moslems to death.
newsitem.headline: Algerian court condemns eight Moslems to death.

text.p: An Algerian court condemned eight Moslem fundamentalist fugitives to death at the weekend for belonging to "an armed terrorist group aiming to spread death", the official Algerian news agency APS said on Sunday.
It said the death sentences were passed in absentia on the eight on Saturday by the court sitting in Medea, 60 km (40 miles) southwest of Algiers.
Earlier this month, the agency said the same court had sentenced 23 Islamists to death, also in their absence.

They were accused of crimes including "belonging to an armed movement, undermining state security, taking part in premeditated murder, sabotage and arson of economic units and educational establishments."

Algerian authorities have been locked in conflict with Moslem fundamentalists since early 1992. Violence started in the North African country shortly after the authorities cancelled a general election in which Islamists had swept to a commanding lead in the first round.
